subject: Evaluation roadmap, MAP milestones, and SLA-linked commercial terms
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novara.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation request + initial timeline

Dylan / Marissa —

Thanks for yesterday's demo. Novara is keen to validate latency and cost claims against a small pilot. Attached is a short evaluation request outlining our objectives and a list of representative workloads. High level asks:

- Proof of 95th pct request latency for streaming responses (target: <= 300ms) over our conversational workload (see attachment).
- Embedding throughput for batch jobs (10k docs/day).
- Typical per-token cost estimates for sustained peak of 40 RPS.

We'd like a mutual action plan (MAP) so both teams know the milestones, acceptance criteria, and who owns what. Ideal timeline: pilot start 02/15, evaluation complete by 03/05, procurement/PO in place by 03/19.

Can you confirm the earliest you can start and whether Redwood can commit to a latency SLA for pilot acceptance? Also attaching a short procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Ari
VP Product, Novara AI

Attachments: 2026-02-03_novara-eval-request.pdf (PDF, 68KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novara.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 11:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation request + initial timeline

Ari —

Appreciate the clear asks and the example payloads. We're aligned on an MAP; attached is a draft we kicked off internally with proposed milestones and success metrics. Summary below:

MAP (draft)
- Week 0 (02/15): Environment provisioning + test data push (owner: Novara / Redwood infra help).
- Week 1 (02/22): Synthetic load run + latency baseline (acceptance: 95th pct p99 <= 320ms for streaming, p50 <= 120ms).
- Week 2 (03/01): Real workload run + cost estimate (acceptance: embeddings throughput >= 10k/day).
- Week 3 (03/05): Final evaluation report + commercial term sheet draft.

Commercial tie-ins we propose now (high level):
- If Redwood meets the MAP acceptance criteria by 03/05, Novara signs a 12-month reserved commit (details to be negotiated) starting 04/01.
- Pricing tier: base list price with a 15% discount if committed monthly GPU-hours >= 2,000 in Q2.
- SLA concessions: Redwood will include an SLO addendum for p95 latency for the primary model path; deeper financial credits / higher discounts require an enterprise SLA and larger commit.

Notes: the latency numbers above are conservative to account for your production payload variability. Marissa — I copied you to start commercial discussions. Laura — please review the SLA language in the attached term sheet; we may need legal on both sides involved if Novara requests financial credits tied to missed p95.

I'll set up a brief MAP sync for Monday 02/09 to walk through the draft.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-02-06_map-draft.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novara.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Evaluation request + initial timeline

Ari — thanks for syncing last week. Quick follow-up from commercial:

- We can offer a conditional commercial concession tied to the MAP: if the MAP acceptance is met by 03/05, Redwood will extend a one-time onboarding discount of 10% off list for the first three months of the committed term.
- For a stronger discount (15%) we would need a Q2 commit (2,000 GPU-hours) and a signed contract by 03/19.
- Regarding SLA: we are comfortable including an SLO for the pilot acceptance criteria (non-binding during pilot). For any financial remedies (credits) tied to p95/p99 latency, that requires an enterprise SLA and procurement approval.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm MAP milestones and acceptance criteria on 02/09 MAP sync.
2) Redwood to run the synthetic baseline by 02/22 and share detailed latency histogram.
3) If MAP acceptance achieved by 03/05, commercial term sheet with listed discounts gets circulated for Novara signature by 03/12.

Ari — can you confirm your internal procurement timeline so we know whether 03/19 contract execution is realistic?

Thanks,
Marissa
Commercial Director | Redwood Inference

From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novara.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation request + initial timeline

Marissa — good summary. Procurement note: our legal/procurement teams are flexible on a 03/19 signature if the MAP is demonstrably on-track. Our inner approvals depend on the MAP acceptance report. We can commit to expedited review if the latency histograms and cost estimates look good on 03/05.

One request on SLA language: Novara's platform is customer-facing; we need an explicit p95 SLO for the primary model path (chat inference). We're proposing target p95 <= 250ms for the pilot's production-like traffic sample. If Redwood cannot meet that, we want clear fallback language in the MAP (e.g., extended evaluation period or additional engineering assistance) rather than immediate financial penalties.

Also, can Redwood outline what level of financial credit structure you would consider if we later move to an enterprise SLA? Having a headline framework helps procurement (e.g., credits as % of monthly committed spend for sustained SLA breaches >2 consecutive weeks).

Appreciate the pragmatic approach — we'll review the draft term sheet and aim to confirm timelines by end of week.

—Ari

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@novara.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation request + initial timeline

Ari / team —

Thanks for the clear ask on SLO language. A few legal-commercial clarifications from Redwood:

- Pilot SLO: we can include a non-binding p95 target of <= 250ms for the pilot evaluation, noted in the MAP as an acceptance criterion. That will be explicitly labeled as "pilot acceptance SLO" and will not carry financial credits.
- Enterprise SLA: if Novara requests financial credits tied to p95 in a post-pilot enterprise SLA, our standard framework is:
  - Tier 1 breach (p95 degraded but availability unaffected): 3% credit of monthly committed spend per full week of sustained breach after a 7-day cure period.
  - Tier 2 breach (p95 degradation impacting availability/throughput): 10% credit per full week after cure period, escalating to contract review if >3 consecutive weeks.

- Important: any financial credits or higher discounts requested as commercial concessions must be coupled with corresponding committed capacity (e.g., the 2,000 GPU-hours Q2 commit) and an agreed incident reporting and mitigation plan in the SLA.

We will put the exact wording into the SLA term-sheet (attached) and mark pilot vs enterprise obligations clearly. If Novara prefers a different credit framework, please propose numbers and we'll take back to our legal.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-02-10_sla-term-sheet.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
